column1: # Requirements of draft-fossil-artifact-format-01, one per row, written from
# the draft text. Columns: ID, section, requirement, optional scope note
# (what the cases leave out). Requirements that cannot be observed in a
# library (UI, wording, IANA, informative text) are not listed. The -01
# erratum is applied in the draft; it is pinned for the fossil(1) 2.28

column3: An artifact's name is the hash of its exact stored bytes, with nothing added, removed or transformed; a signed artifact's name covers its wrapper.
A 40-digit name is the SHA-1, and a 64-digit name the SHA3-256 (FIPS 202, not Keccak), of the raw bytes.
A candidate name of any length other than 40 or 64 is invalid.
Every name an implementation computes or emits is lowercase hexadecimal.
A parser that accepts an uppercase-hex name does not case-normalize it.
Verification compares a name byte for byte with the lowercase digest its length selects; any other length, an uppercase digit or a mismatch never verifies.
The raw input is non-empty and its last byte is LF, checked before any signature wrapper is removed.
The stripped content is at least 10 bytes, starts with a letter A-Z, and has a space as its second byte.
Bytes left unconsumed after the card loop cause rejection.
A PGP clearsign wrapper is removed before parsing.
An SSH signed-message wrapper is removed before parsing.
A wrapper is removed only when the first 34 bytes of the input are exactly one of the two header lines.
The body starts after the first blank line (LF LF or LF CR LF); with no blank line nothing is stripped.
The content is cut after the LF that starts the last signature-armor line, and runs to the end of input when there is none.
Only the first 29 bytes of the 30-byte signature-armor literal are compared.
A sterilized artifact, its marker line after the final card or before a signature block, is rejected by the card-ordering rule.
The byte after a card letter is exactly a space or LF; any other byte, tab included, makes the card invalid.
Tokens are split on space and LF only; tab and CR are ordinary token bytes.
A card's final token may be empty (the line ends in a space), giving a present, empty value distinct from an omitted token; an empty token anywhere else is malformed.
A card with more tokens than its grammar defines is rejected.
A card letter outside A-Z is rejected.
The undefined letters O, S, V, X and Y are rejected.
The eight escapes \n \s \t \r \v \f \0 and \\ decode to LF, space, tab, CR, VT, FF, NUL and backslash.
A backslash before any other byte decodes to that byte, and a token's final backslash is kept; neither is an error.
Tokens are decoded at the A filename and target, C comment, F filename and old-name, H title, J value, L title, N mimetype, T name and value, and U login.
No other token is decoded: hashes, checksums, timestamps, the J field name, and the W size and body stay raw.
The A target is decoded before it is validated, so an escaped token that decodes to hex digits is checked as a hash.
Each card's letter is greater than or equal to the previous card's letter.
An N card directly after a P card is accepted once an E card has been seen, and rejected otherwise.
A second A, B, C, D, E, G, H, I, K, L, N, R, U or W card is rejected.
F, J, M, T, P and Q cards may repeat, each adding to its list.
The Z card has no duplicate guard: an earlier Z line is content covered by the final checksum.
F cards are strictly ascending by decoded filename.
J cards are strictly ascending by field name.
M cards are strictly ascending by hash.
T cards ascend by the full name token, sign included, and strictly by target among equal names.
P tokens keep their order and are not deduplicated.
Q cards are neither ordered nor checked for duplicates.
The canonical comparator compares unsigned bytes with no case folding or normalization; a prefix sorts first and '/' is not special.

A decoded A filename, F filename or F old-name is rejected when empty, starting with '/', '.' or '..' alone, starting with './' or '../', containing '//', ending in '/', or with a '.' or '..' element.
The pathname predicate rejects nothing else: backslashes, spaces, control bytes and invalid UTF-8 pass.
A writer does not create a filename containing a backslash or outside the UTF-8 profile.
A decoded wiki name is rejected when its first byte is 0x20 or below, a later byte is below 0x20, it has two adjacent spaces, it ends in a space, or it is not 1 to 100 bytes long.
A wiki name is otherwise unconstrained: 0x7F, bytes 0x80 and above, and invalid UTF-8 pass.
An F card whose decoded filename is reserved (_FOSSIL_ or .fslckout, whole or after '/', or followed by -wal, -shm or -journal) is dropped, not rejected.
A reserved tail that is neither whole, after '/', nor followed by a sidecar suffix is not reserved, and the old-name is never tested.
The F sort check runs before the drop, and a dropped card never becomes the anchor for the next comparison.
A dropped F card assigns no artifact type and records no file entry.
A writer emits D and E timestamps as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with an optional fraction.
A parser accepts a date-time with T or whitespace separators, HH:MM with optional seconds and a fraction of any length, and an optional +HH:MM, -HH:MM, Z or z zone.
A lowercase t separator is rejected.
In the date-time, date-only and time-only forms, the year is 4 digits, month 01-12, day 01-31 with no calendar check, hour 00-24, minute and second 00-59.
A date on or before -4713-11-24 is rejected.
A Julian day number is an optional sign, digits with an optional fraction (at least one digit), and an optional E or e exponent with an optional sign; no other numeric spelling is recognized.
A Julian day number that is zero, negative, or 5373484.5 or more, after rounding to the nearest millisecond, is rejected.
Every hash position (A target as a hash, A source, B, E ID, F hash, G, I, M, P, both Q tokens, T target) holds exactly 40 or 64 hexadecimal digits.
The K ticket ID is exactly 40 hexadecimal digits; 64 is invalid.
Only the final path component of the A filename is kept as the attachment name.
The A target is a valid hash or a well-formed wiki name.
The A source is optional and none is recorded when absent; a present but empty source fails hash validation and is rejected.
A delta manifest whose baseline is itself a delta manifest is accepted, and its file set is computed from that baseline's own F cards only.
A C card with no token at all (a bare C line) is rejected.
A C card whose single token is empty is a present, empty comment and is accepted.
An E card carries a timestamp and a technote ID.
In a baseline manifest every F card carries a hash; a hashless F card needs a B card.
The third F token is the raw permission, accepted without validation; only the fourth is the old-name.
A producer that writes an old-name also writes an explicit permission token.
An absent J value is the empty string.
A writer emits the K ticket ID in lowercase.
An empty P card is accepted.
The first Q token is + or - followed by a hash; the optional second is a plain hash, empty when absent.
A T name starts with +, - or *.
A T name is not entirely hexadecimal after its sign, at any length and in either case.
A T target is a hash or exactly '*'.
An absent T value is distinct from a present, empty one (erratum 4.2).
A U card with an empty or omitted login yields the login "anonymous".
The W body is exactly size bytes, may hold any byte including LF, and is not scanned for card boundaries.
The byte after the W body is LF.
A reader takes only the leading digits of the W size token, so 4x is 4 and abc is 0.
A W size beyond the rest of the artifact, or one that overflows, is rejected.
Every structural artifact is classified as exactly one of the eight types.
An artifact with a card outside its type's allowed set is rejected.
An artifact missing a card of its type's required set is rejected.
When several type-setting cards appear, the last one processed sets the type.
With no type-setting card, an artifact with a C or P card is a manifest, and any other a control artifact.
An artifact whose every F card was dropped for a reserved filename, with no C or P card, is a control artifact and is rejected for its F card.
A control artifact has no self-referential T card.
Every T card in a technote is self-referential and has the + sign.
A forum post does not have both an H card and an I card.
A forum post's P card lists at most one parent.
The R and Z tokens are exactly 32 hexadecimal digits.
An artifact whose Z card does not match is rejected.
The Z value is compared, byte for byte, with the lowercase MD5 of the stripped content before its last 35 bytes, so an uppercase digit fails.
An artifact without a Z card is rejected.
A producer writes the Z card as Z, a space, 32 lowercase digits and LF.
The Z verification stage does not itself reject an artifact for lacking a Z card, or for being too short to hold one.
The Z verifier neither reads nor requires any value at the artifact's last byte.
A parser does not check the R value against file content.
The R value is the MD5 of, for each file in comparator order, its name, a space, its decimal size, LF and its content, written as 32 lowercase digits.
A delta manifest's R value covers the merged file set, not its own F cards.
A writer emits the R card as R, a space, 32 lowercase digits and LF.
At commit time the R card is checked byte for byte against the lowercase digest recomputed from the checkout.
column4: No case: go-libfossil has no commit-time check to observe. Its commit computes the R card from the tree it is writing, so the digest is lowercase by construction (AF-6.3-4); fossil(1) cannot be made to hold an uppercase R card at commit.

column3: New content is named SHA-1 under sha1 and auto, and SHA3-256 under sha3, sha3-only and shun-sha1.
Policy value strings match case-sensitively and exactly; an unrecognized value is a fatal error.
column4: No case: go-libfossil reads and writes only the ordinal in the hash-policy setting and has no surface that takes a value string (fossil's is the hash-policy command), so there is nothing to feed a wrong-case or unknown name.

column3: With no policy set, a repository holding a SHA3 name or no SHA-1 name, including an empty one, defaults to sha3, and otherwise to auto.
Under auto, storing an artifact under a name longer than 40 digits promotes the repository to sha3 and persists the change.
Under sha1, auto and sha3, content already stored under the other algorithm's name keeps that name and is not stored again.
Under sha3-only and shun-sha1, content is named SHA3-256 even when it is already stored under a SHA-1 name.
Changing the policy never renames a stored artifact.
A manifest is a delta manifest exactly when it has a B card, and its file set is the merge with its baseline.
In the merge, a delta entry with a hash replaces or adds a file, a hashless entry deletes it, other baseline files carry forward, and an unmatched deletion adds nothing.
Enumerating a delta manifest's files fails when its baseline is missing or is not a manifest.
Looking up one name in a delta manifest searches the delta first, and a delete marker answers not-found without reading the baseline.
